decisions: The whole brief was written under the operator's delegation of 2026-11-02 for the #81-#88 chain. The operator should confirm the delegation covers these choices.
Change the plan skill, not the gate review's standard: agree. docs/design-notes/copilot-cli-experiments.md:549-592 shows the gate review was right (8 of 9 gates imported internal modules).
A pin stays allowed where no named surface reaches the criterion, stated in the task's acceptance: agree. After the edit, Naming, pins-unnamed and not-contract say the same thing.
G1 replaces the whole paragraph and drops 'Do not pin a name that no gate uses.'; 'the minimum a gate needs, and no more' covers it. Fine.

G2 ('until the finding no longer holds') gives the planner no exit for a check-gap it cannot close (the 2026-11-02 run ended on one). Acceptable here; worth a follow-up that tells the planner to leave a check-gap standing and report it.
gpt-6.1-terra is the only candidate; the others wait for #81. Fine.
Qualification is the operator's acceptance at close, and #84 closes only if every phase qualifies. Necessary: sessions have no network.
Only the gate-review ceiling rises (1550 to 1600; about 1564 words after G3). Plan ends at about 3,930 of 4,100. Fine.
The eval's brief rules out gate folders, so the single-file llm grader sees every judge; its library is a shell library. Fine.
Acceptance 1 runs each case once and reruns from 7de2855 only below 1.00: cheap but noisy. The operator's call.
